def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    𝓑 ⊢ F (∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥ →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K (∼F ⊥))
a_raw: {"translation": "`Target` is defined as the proposition asserting that for all types `Fm`, `S₀`, and `S`, all choices of logical connectives (`LogicalConnective Fm`) and truth/falsehood constants (`LogicalNeutral Fm`) on `Fm`, all entailment (provability) relations for `S₀` and `S` over `Fm` (`Entailment S₀ Fm` and `Entailment S Fm`), all proof systems `𝓑 : S₀` and `𝓢 : S` satisfying classical propositional logic (`Entailment.Cl 𝓑` and `Entailment.Cl 𝓢`, meaning each proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens), and all functions `K : Fm → Fm` and `F : Fm → Fm`, if the following five hypotheses hold: (1) `Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K`, i.e., for every `φ : Fm`, if `𝓑 ⊢ φ` then `𝓢 ⊢ K φ`; (2) `Def2 𝓢 K`, i.e., for all `φ, ψ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ)`; (3) `Def4 𝓢 K`, i.e., for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 φ)`; (4) `𝓑 ⊢ F (∼(F ⊥)) 🡒 F ⊥`; and (5) for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)`; then `𝓢 ⊢ K (∼(K (∼(F ⊥))))`. Nothing else is assumed: in particular, neither `Def3 𝓢 K` (`∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡒 φ`) nor `Def5 𝓑 F` (`∃ ψ, 𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ)`) is required, neither `𝓑` nor `𝓢` is assumed to be consistent, `K` is not assumed to satisfy necessitation within `𝓢` itself (`𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ`), and no other axioms or rules are assumed for `F` or for the relationship between `𝓑` and `𝓢`."}
translation: `Target` is defined as the proposition asserting that for all types `Fm`, `S₀`, and `S`, all choices of logical connectives (`LogicalConnective Fm`) and truth/falsehood constants (`LogicalNeutral Fm`) on `Fm`, all entailment (provability) relations for `S₀` and `S` over `Fm` (`Entailment S₀ Fm` and `Entailment S Fm`), all proof systems `𝓑 : S₀` and `𝓢 : S` satisfying classical propositional logic (`Entailment.Cl 𝓑` and `Entailment.Cl 𝓢`, meaning each proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens), and all functions `K : Fm → Fm` and `F : Fm → Fm`, if the following five hypotheses hold: (1) `Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K`, i.e., for every `φ : Fm`, if `𝓑 ⊢ φ` then `𝓢 ⊢ K φ`; (2) `Def2 𝓢 K`, i.e., for all `φ, ψ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ)`; (3) `Def4 𝓢 K`, i.e., for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 φ)`; (4) `𝓑 ⊢ F (∼(F ⊥)) 🡒 F ⊥`; and (5) for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)`; then `𝓢 ⊢ K (∼(K (∼(F ⊥))))`. Nothing else is assumed: in particular, neither `Def3 𝓢 K` (`∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡒 φ`) nor `Def5 𝓑 F` (`∃ ψ, 𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ)`) is required, neither `𝓑` nor `𝓢` is assumed to be consistent, `K` is not assumed to satisfy necessitation within `𝓢` itself (`𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ`), and no other axioms or rules are assumed for `F` or for the relationship between `𝓑` and `𝓢`.

divergences.description: TARGET adds the explicit hypothesis `𝓑 ⊢ F (∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥` (the formalized second incompleteness theorem for `F`), which is absent from the source passage. The passage states Theorem 4 with no such proviso and immediately beforehand stresses that `F(x)` can be any formula in `L_EA` with one free variable. Although the printed theorem for an arbitrary formula `F(x)` indeed fails without some condition on `F` (e.g., `F(x) := (x ≠ ⌜⊥⌝)` under `Con(F) := ¬F(⌜⊥⌝)`), inserting formalized Gödel II for `F` directly as a premise materially weakens the theorem relative to the text and reduces what is established to a purely propositional modal transfer under `K`.

TARGET uses a purely abstract propositional setting (`Fm`, `S₀`, `S`, and arbitrary functions `K, F : Fm → Fm`), so it cannot express concrete arithmetic (`EA`), Gödel numbering (`⌜φ⌝`), object-language quantifiers, or the syntactic notion of a one-free-variable formula `F(x)` in `L_EA` (or its contrast with `Σ⁰₁` provability predicates). Because `Target` universally quantifies over all such abstract structures, this is an idealization/generalization that covers the concrete setting as an instance (modulo the added hypothesis).

The source passage leaves `Con(F)` undefined on the page, whereas TARGET fixes it to `∼F ⊥`. This is the standard provability-logic reading (`¬F(⌜⊥⌝)`), though for an arbitrary formula `F(x)` not closed under logic it is not equivalent to other definitions of consistency.

Instead of assuming that `S` includes `EA` (Epistemic Arithmetic), TARGET does not require `𝓢` to prove all theorems of `𝓑` (nor factivity `Def3`, positive introspection, or necessitation in `𝓢`), assuming only classical propositional logic in `𝓑` and `𝓢` plus `Def1` (`𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ`), `Def2` (`K`-distribution), and `Def4` (known factivity). Since these are consequences of `S` including `EA`, this is a harmless strengthening (weakening of the hypotheses on `𝓑`, `𝓢`, and `K`).

judgement.summary: TARGET accurately translates the premise `∀ φ, S ⊢ K(Kφ → F(⌜φ⌝))` and conclusion `S ⊢ K¬K(Con(F))` of Theorem 4 into an abstract modal setting with `Con(F) := ∼F ⊥`, but it diverges materially from the source passage by adding the formalized second incompleteness theorem for `F` (`𝓑 ⊢ F (∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥`) as an explicit hypothesis not present in the text. Even though the printed theorem for arbitrary `F(x)` genuinely needs some extra condition on `F`, assuming formalized Gödel II outright makes the formal statement materially weaker than—and qualitatively different from—the source claim.
